Renewable energy sources like solar, wind, and hydroelectric power are increasingly central to global efforts to reduce carbon emissions. Unlike fossil fuels, these sources replenish naturally and produce little to no greenhouse gas during operation. Solar photovoltaic costs have fallen dramatically over the past decade, making it one of the cheapest forms of new electricity generation in many regions. Wind power, both onshore and offshore, complements solar by often generating more during different times of day and seasons. The main challenges remaining are grid integration, energy storage at scale, and ensuring a just transition for workers and communities currently dependent on fossil fuel industries.
